narrative:
The model estimates you have a 49% chance of leaving your job. This is high enough that the company has decided to deny your promotion, as they are concerned you may not stay long-term.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile. First, your total years of experience across all jobs had the strongest influence, pulling the prediction toward you staying. Most employees the model expects to stay have similar short experience levels of 1-5 years, so in this respect you look like a typical long-term employee. 

However, two other factors pushed more strongly toward leaving. The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important driver, increasing the likelihood you will depart. Additionally, working in the medical sector also contributed to the prediction of leaving, even though medical is one of the more common sectors among employees expected to remain.

Taken together, the combination of external opportunities and your industry outweighed the stabilizing effect of your experience level, leading to the decision against promotion.

The organization should discuss with you what would increase your commitment and address any concerns raised by those external offers. You may want to reflect on whether the medical sector continues to align with your long-term goals. Open dialogue about career development could help retain talent like yours. (218 words)
